# Turnstone

> Turnstone is a single-page, zero-backend workspace for *lists*: load a list of links (or a list with no links at all), work through it as task cards with statuses and notes, and save progress back to the file. It reads CSV, TSV, XLSX/XLS/ODS, DOCX tables, Markdown, JSON, HTML tables, XML feeds, `.eml`/`.mht` email, and a pasted clipboard table. It runs entirely in the browser — no upload, no account, no server — and every dependency is vendored.

This file exists so an agent can use Turnstone without reading its source. The single most useful thing here is **workspace links**: a URL that carries a list, so an agent that has found or generated a list can hand over one link that opens it as a ready-to-work queue.

## Workspace links — a whole list inside a URL

Open `https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/app.html` followed by `#` and a payload:

- `#data=<percent-encoded list>` — plain text. Small, human-readable, easy to construct by hand or with a URL encoder. Best for a handful of rows.
- `#zdata=<payload>` — the list deflated with **raw** deflate and base64url-encoded with no padding. Four to six times smaller; use this for anything real.
- `&sum=<length>.<hash>` — optional integrity token: the byte length and an FNV-1a 32-bit hash of the list's UTF-8 bytes, each in base 36, joined by a dot. Verified when present (a truncated link is refused rather than opening a shorter queue), ignored when absent.
- `&format=csv|tsv|json|md|xml|html` — force the reader instead of sniffing.
- `&link=<portal template>` — compose each row's link from its own values, for lists with no links of their own: `&link=https://portal.example.com/incident/{Ticket}`. `{Column}` is percent-encoded into the URL, `{Column|raw}` is spliced verbatim, `{0}` addresses a column by position. Only an `http(s)` result is ever turned into a link.
- `&name=<label>` — what to call the workspace in the sidebar.
- `&open=1` — open the first task as soon as the link loads.

To build one, in any language, with no service or key:

```
raw   = utf8_bytes(list)
sum   = base36(len(raw)) + "." + base36(fnv1a32(raw))
zdata = base64url(deflate_raw(raw), padding=none)
url   = "https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/app.html#zdata=" + zdata + "&sum=" + sum
```

The deflate stream must be **raw** (no zlib or gzip wrapper). In Node: `zlib.deflateRawSync(b).toString('base64url')`. In Python: `zlib.compressobj(9, zlib.DEFLATED, -15)` then `base64.urlsafe_b64encode(...).rstrip(b'=')`. In a browser: `CompressionStream('deflate-raw')`.

**fnv1a32 must be a true 32-bit multiply.** In JavaScript use `Math.imul` — the naive `h = (h * 0x01000193) >>> 0` computes the product in float64, and once it passes 2^53 the low bits round away, so the hash silently disagrees with Turnstone's and any link with a `sum` built that way is refused. In Python and other languages with native 32-bit ints, a plain multiply-and-mask works: `h = ((h ^ byte) * 0x01000193) & 0xFFFFFFFF`.

A worked example, carrying four rows and no portal address:

```
https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/app.html#data=Name%2CURL%0AApple%20Newsroom%2Chttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.apple.com%2Fnewsroom%2F%0AGitHub%20Trending%2Chttps%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Ftrending
```

Notes that matter when generating these:

- Put the payload in the **fragment**, not the query string. A fragment is never sent to a server, so the list stays private, and it escapes the ~8 KB request-line limit that would make a long `?data=` fail at the host. `?data=` is still read, for tooling that can only append a query.
- Prefer `#data=` when the list is short enough that percent-encoding is smaller than base64 of a deflate stream — roughly under a kilobyte. It is also the only one a person can read.
- A list is text. CSV with a header row works best, because the header names the columns, but a plain list of links (one per line), a Markdown task list, a JSON array of objects, or a TSV block all work.
- There is no need to URL-encode the payload twice, and no escaping of the list's content is required beyond the encoding above.
- Limits: Turnstone refuses more than 2 MB of list and warns past 100 KB, because a chat or mail client trims long links. Rows are not capped.

## What Turnstone reads

CSV, TSV, XLSX, XLS, XLSM, XLSB, ODS, DOCX (Word tables), Markdown (task lists and pipe tables), JSON (an array of objects, or an array nested one level down), HTML tables, XML feeds (RSS, Atom, sitemaps, OPML), `.eml`/`.mht` email (a table in the body, or a spreadsheet attached to one), and a table pasted from the clipboard. The link column is chosen from the **values** rather than the headers, so a URL, an email address or a phone number all work as the thing a row opens. CSV, TSV and XLSX can be written back to in place; the rest are read-only sources.

## Which edition to hand it to

Every edition reads a workspace link: the web app (`app.html`), the standalone single-file build and the bookmarklet open one from a URL, and the **Chrome extension** takes one pasted into its side panel — either into the field on its first screen, or through **☰ → Open a workspace link…**, which works while another list is open. A **data file** (CSV, TSV, XLSX) works on the extension too.

What you cannot do is *drive* the extension: a side panel is worked by a person in a real Chrome window, and an agent in a sandbox, in a headless browser or on another machine has no such panel. So hand the list over — as a link, or as a file when the user prefers — and the user opens it. Never assume you can work their queue.

## Files

- [Overview](https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/index.html.md): what Turnstone is, in Markdown — features, editions, and the questions people ask.
- [Share a list as a link](https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/workspace-link.html.md): the workspace-link format in full, with recipes in Node, Python and the browser, and the reasoning behind the fragment.
- [All editions](https://spuds0588.github.io/Turnstone/versions.html): which build to use — web app, offline single file, bookmarklet, or Chrome extension.
- [README](https://github.com/Spuds0588/Turnstone/blob/main/README.md): the repository's own overview, including every supported format and how detection works.
- [Sample lists](https://github.com/Spuds0588/Turnstone/tree/main): `sample-links.csv`, `sample-links.xlsx`, `sample-links.md`, `sample-links.docx` and the workflow fixtures are all one ten-row queue in different containers, and are good material for a workspace link.
